rules.sentence: Brucellosis can present with features based on the underlying syndrome, including meningoencephalitis, myelitis, transaminitis, orchitis, epididymitis, endocarditis, sacroiliitis, spondylodiscitis, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, epidural abscesses, and hepatic abscesses.
Respiratory symptoms can include cough, breathlessness, and pleurisy, with focal lung abscesses and pleural effusions reported.
Guillain-Barré syndrome and Subarachnoid hemorrhage have been reported in acute neurobrucellosis.
Dermatological manifestations include maculopapular rashes, erythema nodosum, cutaneous abscesses, and panniculitis.
Endocarditis and aortic fistulas are rare.
Although lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and features of an underlying syndrome may be present, the physical examination may be normal.
Brucellosis frequently presents as a fever of unknown origin, prompting a significant workup before diagnosis.
The mortality rate ranges from 2% to 5%.
